CARBIDE TIPS 

PART 4 CARBIDE TIPS FOR MULTI POINT TOOLS - SPECIFICATION 

UDC 62r9025 [ 669'018'25 ] 



® BIS 1993 

BUREAU OF INDIAN STANDARDS 

MANAK BHAVAN, 9 BAHADUR SHAH ZAFAR MARG 
NEW DELHI 110002 

April 1993 Price Gronp 3 



Single Point Cutting Tools, Carbide Tips and Indexable Inserts Sectional Committee, PE 12 



FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Single Point Cutting Tools, Carbide Tips and Indexable Inserts Sectional Committee had been 
approved by the Production Engineering Division Council. 

Dimensions and other requirements of carbide tips for cutting tools were covered in dififerent 
Indian Standards as listed below: 

IS 2162 : 1979 Dimensions of carbide tips for single point tools 

IS 8065 : 1976 Dimensions of carbide tips for light cutting operations 

IS 8301 : 1976 Dimensions of carbide tips for drills with point angle 115** ( Type AB ) 

IS 9327 : 1V79 Dimensions of carbide tips for reamers, core drills, end mills and slot 
milling cutters 

IS 12294 : 1988 Dimensions of carbide tips for parting off and turning tools for sliding head 
type automats ( IND 5 and IND 6 ) 

It has been decided to cover all the above carbide tips under one Indian Standard in different 
parts for quick and ease of reference. Hence all the above standards have been combined in one 
standard having seven parts. Carbide tips for round nose turning tools have also been covered ia 
part seven of the standard. The other Indian Standards on carbide tips of this series are: 

IS 13741 ( Part 1 ) Carbide tips for single point tools 

IS 13741 ( Part 2 ) Carbide tips for single point tools for light cutting operations 

IS 13741 ( Part 3 ) Carbide tips for single point tool blanks for sliding head type automates 

IS 13741 ( Part 5 ) Carbide tips for twist drills with point angle 115° 

IS 13741 ( Part 6 ) Carbide tips for single point threading tools 

IS 13741 ( Part 7 ) Carbide tips for single point round nose turning tools 

The types have been so arranged in different parts so that review and updating becomes easier 
when the referred ISO or National Standard is updated. 

In the preparation of this standard, considerable assistance has been derived from DIN 8011 : 1963 
'Carbide tips for reamers, countersinks, counterbores and end mills' issued by Deutsches Institut 
fiir Normung ( DIN ). 

The type BR has been included in line with SMS ( Swedish ) Standard. 

These carbide tips are used on multi point tools covered in: 

IS 9322 : 1980 Technical supply conditions for carbide tipped milling cutters 

IS 9323 : 1991 Specification for carbide tipped end mills with parallel shanks {first 

revision) 

IS 9324 : 1991 Specification for carbide tipped end mills with morse taper and tapped end 

shanks ( second revision ) 
IS 9771 : 1981 Specification for carbide tipped core drills with morse taper shanks 

IS 10884 : 1984 Specification for carbide tipped chucking reamers with parallel shanks 
IS 10885 : 1984 Specification for carbide tipped chucking reamers with morse taper shank 
IS 11934 : 1987 Specification for carbide tipped shell reamers 
IS 11935 : 1987 Specification for carbide tipped chucking reamers with morse taper shank 

with long cutting edge 

IS 11936 : 1987 Specification for carbide tipped long fluted machine reamer with morse 
taper shank. 

This standard supersedes IS 9327 t 1979. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with^ 
the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in 
accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values ( rev/^eJ)*. The number 
of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified 
value in this standard. 



IS 13741 ( Part 4 ) : 1993 



Indian Standard 
CARBIDE TIPS 

PART 4 CARBIDE TIPS FOR MULTI POINT TOOLS —SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

This standard covers the dimensions and other 
requirements for carbide tips for reamers, end 
mills, slot milling cutters and core drills. 

2 REFERENCE 

IS 2428 : 1964 * Application of carbides for 
machining, ranges of application and colour 
code' is necessary adjunct to this standard. 

3 TYPES 

Carbide tips for single point tools shall be of 



following types: 

Type R — for reamers 

Type BR — for reamers 

Type T — for end mill and slot milling 
cutters 

Type U — for slot milling cutters 
Type V — for core drills 

4 DIMENSIONS 

The dimensions of carbide tips shall be as 
given in Tables 1 to 5 read with respective 
figures corresponding to each type.

5 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 

5.1 Carbide tips shall be free from cracks. 

6 DESIGNATION 

Carbide tips shall be designated by carbide tip 
type, length (/) IS No. and range of application 
as per IS 2428 : 1964. 

Carbide tip of Type U have length (/) 22 mm 
and with range of application K 20 and 



conforming to this standard, shall be designated 
as: 

Carbide tip IS 13741 ( Part 4 ) U 22 K 20 

7 MARKING 

Shall be marked with designation, manufacturer's 
name or trade-mark on the carton. 

8 PACKAGING 

The carbide tips shall be suitably packed to 
avoid damage in handling and transit. 



Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the pro- 
ducer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to 
that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use 
of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtainedjrom 
the Bureau of Indian Standards.
